knowledge_point.title: Computing an Integral Using the Sum Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \left(-y^{3}-2\right)\,\mathrm{d}y &= \int \left(-y^{3}-2\right)\,\mathrm{d}y \\ &= -\int y^{3}\,\mathrm{d}y-2\int 1\,\mathrm{d}y \\ &= -\frac{y^{3+1}}{(3+1)}-2\frac{y^{0+1}}{(0+1)}+C \\ &= -\frac{y^{4}}{4}-2y+C\end{aligned}
$$
